title: Are they anagrams?
prompt:
Write anagrams(a, b) that returns True if the two texts use exactly the same letters the same number of times, ignoring capital letters and spaces.
Example: 'Listen' and 'Silent' -> True.
hints: What must be true of two words for them to be anagrams? Think about the letters and how many of each.
Two texts have the same letters exactly when, after sorting their letters, the results are equal. Which small clean-up must happen before you sort?
Plan: for each text remove spaces, make it lower case, sort its letters; return whether the two sorted results are equal. Mind 'aab' vs 'abb': a set of letters isn't enough, counts matter.

edge_hints.uppercase: 'L' and 'l' differ for Python; convert the case first.
edge_hints.spaces: Spaces are not letters; remove them before comparing.
edge_hints.duplicates: Comparing sets of letters ignores how many times each appears. Compare sorted letters or counts instead.
edge_hints.empty: Two empty texts have the same (no) letters: True.
